previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old female was admitted for nausea and vomiting lasting six days, with inability to tolerate oral intake and associated dehydration. She also reported urinary frequency and urgency, left lower quadrant pain, and worsening fibromyalgia pain. Initial concerns included bowel obstruction and low phenytoin levels due to missed doses. Abdominal imaging showed no obstruction. She was treated with IV fluids, antiemetics, and IV phenytoin, which was later transitioned to oral therapy as levels normalized. A urine culture confirmed Proteus mirabilis urinary tract infection, treated with ciprofloxacin. Her nausea improved with Reglan and bowel rest, and she gradually resumed oral intake. Pain was managed with IV then oral opioids. She remained seizure-free and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, continue Reglan, and follow up on INR and phenytoin levels in one week.
